name: Brazil
summary: Three national MNOs (Vivo, Claro, TIM) after Oi's mobile business was split between them in 2022, plus regional operators (Algar, Brisanet, Unifique, Amazônia 5G, iez!, Ligga). Most sub-3 GHz licences are regional, so amounts are population-weighted averages computed from Anatel's per-municipality licence acts; national blocks (700, 2.5, 3.5, 26 GHz) are shown with exact edges in separate position views.

operators.name: Vivo
operators.notes: Received ~43 MHz (pop-weighted) of Oi Móvel spectrum when Oi's mobile unit (UPI Ativos Móveis) was split between TIM, Vivo and Claro on 20 Apr 2022. A 2022 700 MHz leasing deal with Winity was conditionally approved but Winity then renounced its licence (end-2023).

operators.name: Claro
operators.notes: América Movil. Absorbed Nextel Brasil (2019). Took Oi customers but essentially no Oi spectrum in the 2022 split (spectrum caps).

operators.name: TIM
operators.notes: Received ~49 MHz (pop-weighted) of Oi Móvel spectrum in the 2022 split, including Oi's 2.5 GHz V2 block per Anatel acts.

operators.name: Algar Telecom
operators.notes: Regional MNO in PGO sectors 3 (Triângulo Mineiro, MG), 22 (MS), 25 (GO) and 33 (Franca, SP) - about 1.6% of the population.

operators.name: Brisanet
operators.notes: Regional 5G entrant (2021 auction: 3.5 GHz Northeast + Centre-West, 2.3 GHz Northeast); won 700 MHz lots A2/A3 (Northeast, Centre-West) on 4 May 2026.

operators.name: Unifique
operators.notes: 3.5 GHz in SC/RS (Consórcio 5G Sul, 2021). Anatel gave prior consent on 7 Apr 2026 for Unifique to take Ligga's 3.5 GHz block in Paraná (completion not confirmed). Bought 56.4% of the Amazônia 5G consortium (Apr 2026). Won 700 MHz lot A4 (South) in May 2026.

operators.name: Amazônia 5G
operators.legal: Amazônia Serviços Digitais e Telecomunicações S.A.
operators.notes: Took over Sercomtel/Ligga's 3.5 GHz block for São Paulo state + North region (transfer published by Anatel, 2025-26). Won 700 MHz lot A1 (North + São Paulo) in May 2026. Unifique bought a 56.4% controlling stake in Apr 2026.

operators.name: iez! telecom
operators.legal: Cloud2u Indústria e Comércio de Equipamentos Eletroeletrônicos Ltda.
operators.notes: Brand of Cloud2U (Greatek group); 3.5 GHz lot C7 (RJ, ES, MG) in 2021; won 700 MHz lot A5 (RJ, ES, MG) in May 2026.

operators.name: Ligga Telecom
operators.notes: Sercomtel (Londrina/Tamarana legacy 850/900/1800) and Copel Telecom rebranded Ligga. Sold its São Paulo/North 3.5 GHz block to Amazônia 5G and agreed (Jan 2026) to sell its Paraná 3.5 GHz block to Unifique (Anatel consent Apr 2026).

bands.label: 700 MHz APT (B28) - per operator
bands.note: TIM, Vivo and Claro hold national 2x10 MHz blocks (2014 auction, expire 8 Dec 2029). The 708-718/763-773 MHz block is regional: Algar in its PGO sectors (2014), and since the 4 May 2026 re-auction of the block Winity returned: Amazônia 5G (North + São Paulo), Brisanet (Northeast, Centre-West), Unifique (South), iez! (RJ/ES/MG); new licences to Dec 2044. The 2026 winners are not yet in Anatel's open-data acts, so their averages are computed from the lot areas. 703-708/758-763 is not assigned on a primary basis (secondary use only).

notes: Method: Anatel open data 'Autorizações e Licenciamento do SMP' (ATOS_SMP.csv, file dated 2026-09-27) lists every primary/secondary SMP radio-frequency act per municipality and sub-band. Primary acts were summed per operator and sub-band and weighted by 2022 census population (IBGE). Acts that expired in 2023-2026 but are under renewal (Claro 1.8/2.1 GHz renewed Q2 2026; TIM/Vivo 850 and some TIM 900/1800 pending) are included.
Figures are MHz per direction for FDD. Pop-weighted totals are approximate and labelled regional-average.

Anatel's acts file is not fully current for recent changes: it still lists Winity's renounced 700 MHz block and Sercomtel's 3.5 GHz block, and does not yet list the May 2026 700 MHz winners. These were corrected from Anatel's auction page, its Q2 2026 competition report and trade press.

Oi Móvel: the UPI split closed 20 Apr 2022; per TeleSíntese TIM got 49 MHz and Vivo 43 MHz (pop-weighted) of Oi's 92 MHz, Claro none. Anatel's acts show ex-Oi 900/1800/2100 blocks now with TIM and Vivo, and Oi's 2.5 GHz V2 with TIM.

Winity: won the national 2x10 MHz 700 MHz lot in 2021; the Vivo leasing deal was approved with conditions but Winity renounced the licence (end-2023; Anatel extinguished it Feb 2024). The block was re-auctioned by region on 4 May 2026 (all lots at the reserve price) to Amazônia 5G, Brisanet, Unifique and iez!; adjudicated 6 May 2026, licences formalised end-May 2026.
3.5 GHz regional block edges conflict: Anatel acts give centre 3640 MHz / 80 MHz (3600-3680), trade press says 3620-3700 MHz. Regulator data used.
Unifique's purchase of Ligga's Paraná 3.5 GHz block had Anatel prior consent on 7 Apr 2026 (valid 180 days); completion not confirmed as of asOf, so Paraná is still shown under Ligga.

Totals sanity check: Anatel's radio-frequency map, as reported by Teletime (Mar 2022, after the 5G auction and before the Oi split), gave Vivo 864, TIM 834 and Claro 684 MHz, apparently counting regional lots at full size. The population-weighted totals here (Vivo ~907, Claro ~702, TIM ~698 MHz) differ mainly because of TIM's regional 26 GHz lots (weighted here) and the 2022 Oi split.
850 MHz: Anatel limited renewals to 2028 because of a planned refarming/re-licensing; the future of the band (including regional operators' interest in 600 MHz) is under debate.
missing: Exact block positions for regionally licensed bands (850, 900, 1800, 2100, 2300, 2.5 GHz P-band) are not drawn - they differ by area; only population-weighted amounts are given.
Neko's 2021 26 GHz regional lot (São Paulo, 200 MHz, 10 years) is absent from Anatel's acts; current status not verified.
Algar sector population share (1.6%) is taken from Algar's 87 municipalities in the 850 MHz acts; regional 3.5 GHz/700 MHz shares use state populations minus those municipalities.
